text:
alex: weird onboarding snag — installed redwoodctl via pip because our dev box already uses pyenv. `redwoodctl login` browser flow succeeds but CLI still asks for device code and my sample-app localtest keeps showing the org demo profile. Any ideas?

priya: can you paste `which redwoodctl` and `redwoodctl --version`? also `echo $REDWOOD_CONFIG` just in case env is pointing somewhere odd.

alex: sure:
```
$ which redwoodctl
/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl
$ redwoodctl --version
redwoodctl 0.35.2
$ echo $REDWOOD_CONFIG
/opt/legacy/redwood/config.yaml
```
I didn't set REDWOOD_CONFIG intentionally. Noticed `/opt/legacy/redwood` contains another team's demo config and tokens.

zack: aha — sounds like PATH vs pyenv mismatch + leftover env var from an older onboarding script. `which` shows /usr/local/bin but your pip-installed binary may be a wrapper that picks up env overrides. localserve and sample-app both check REDWOOD_CONFIG first; if it's set they'll ignore XDG and legacy home paths. That explains the demo profile.

alex: ok so do I unset REDWOOD_CONFIG? Will that break anything else?

priya: quick repro fix: `unset REDWOOD_CONFIG` in your shell, then run `redwoodctl login --force` (force will refresh device flow). Alternatively, point REDWOOD_CONFIG at your user config: `export REDWOOD_CONFIG=~/.config/redwood/config.yaml`. After login, restart sample-app.

alex: unset and re-login worked. localtest now uses my personal profile. But curious — device-code loop happened because CLI saw config file but couldn't write token? there wasn't a permissions error though.

zack: likely two factors: (1) the wrapper binary from pip could be older and handles refresh differently, (2) some installs create auth.cache where the owner is root or a different user, and if CLI can't refresh it it falls back to asking for device code. In your case the leftover /opt/legacy token was stale and unreadable by your user, so CLI thought there was no valid token and started device flow; the browser completed, but the token got written to a different location the sample-app wasn't watching.

alex: bleh. What's a robust fix so new dev boxes don't hit this?

priya: a few items: (A) installer doc should warn about stray REDWOOD_CONFIG in common CI/dev images and avoid setting global env vars, (B) add a `redwoodctl doctor` check that warns when REDWOOD_CONFIG points outside the home dir or when multiple config locations exist, (C) detect wrapper/packaging mismatches and print a hint when `--version` doesn't match expected runtime, (D) localserve/sample-app should log which config path they loaded at startup (and include it in metrics) so it's obvious.

maria: from PM side — adding a small onboarding checklist: check PATH, unset REDWOOD_CONFIG, run `redwoodctl doctor`, then `redwoodctl login`. Also we should update quickstart to recommend installing via our distro packages or Homebrew for now, not pip.

alex: agreed. I can send the exact commands I ran to reproduce. Also noticed `pip` left a stub at `/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` that execs a script in `/usr/local/lib/python*/site-packages/redwoodctl/cli.py` — maybe we should detect if we run from an unexpected site-packages path and warn.

devex-bot: Created issue #5229: "installer/DX: detect legacy REDWOOD_CONFIG env, multiple config paths, and packaging mismatch; add 'redwoodctl doctor' checks and clearer logs". Labels: devex, onboarding, medium-priority.

zack: I'll pick up a small PR to (1) add a doctor check for REDWOOD_CONFIG outside home, (2) print loaded config path on startup at INFO level, (3) add a warning when multiple config directories are present.

priya: also adding a CLI flag `--show-config-paths` that prints all resolved candidate paths, useful for debugging. Could be in v0.36.

alex: thanks all — resolved for my onboarding. Happy to test patches. :thumbsup:
